req.title: Login rejects wrong password
req.statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect password.' error when the password hash comparison fails.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/login must render an 'Incorrect password.' error when the password hash comparison fails. We need: (1) a positive case confirming correct credentials succeed without the error, (2) a negative case confirming wrong password produces exactly 'Incorrect password.' in the response body with HTTP 200, (3) a boundary case distinguishing 'Incorrect password.' from 'Incorrect username.' to ensure the correct branch fires. Additional tests cover the exact error string constant, the boolean branch logic (user found but hash fails vs user not found), and state transitions to kill comparison-flip and string-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_login_correct_password_no_error_message
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with user id=1 username='test' password='test' (hashed)
trace: R-FLASKR-010: correct credentials must NOT trigger the error path
Catches boolean-negation mutation on check_password_hash condition
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_login_correct_password_no_error_message():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert b'Incorrect password.' not in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect username.' not in r.data
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_login_correct_password_no_error_message()
